scope: Isolated Chrome with a frozen 512-match tournament response. All write/server calls simulated. Read-only live response timings measured separately. No player data included.

historical_cause.finding: Header geometry reads lay out intermediate legacy results before board transformation and the existing 50-result visibility limit.

changes: Hide main only during the synchronous ui_show transaction; restore inline display and priority in finally.
Retain the names-layout job while first sizes are unobserved without forcing an otherwise unused computed-style/layout read.
Reuse at most 16 timezone formatters during scheduled-time conversion, retaining the existing conversion algorithm.

comparison.order: before, after, after, before; fresh Chrome sessions; no CPU profiler
comparison.measurement: From response handling (after fixture cloning) until three frames without pending tournament/board jobs. Asset load and server latency excluded.

verification.timezone_regression: Unmodified baseline constructs 1000 formatters for 1000 conversions; candidate constructs one. Golden summer/winter and fractional-hour offsets pass.

installed_startup_smoke.scope: Synthetic isolated startup with 512 games and 423 finished.
checks: All 512 games and 50 visible results survive the initial build
The main view is visible after all startup work
A failed build restores prior inline display and priority
A complete rebuild recovers after failure with every game

verification.synthetic_fixture: Finished games use a fixed midday timestamp so date selection and the 50-result assertion remain deterministic across midnight.

limitations: Two runs per variant on this machine, not a user-device latency guarantee or p99 measurement.
All 512 rows are still built; 50 finished games initially visible. No data/list limit or virtualization added.
Asset/script initialization takes roughly another half second locally; a subsecond full reload is not achieved.
Existing baseline lint findings in cmatch.js and ctournament.js remain, with no added findings.
No backend, database, BTP write path or BUP client changes.
